Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Directional wounds

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The local player receives the original red wound chevron, 30 pixels toward the hit origin, fading over 0.55 seconds. It stays at the location of that hit as the player moves. Spectators and other players do not receive that personal cue.

Hurt.position already means damage origin. The saved collision-proxy history provides the victim's position at the event tick, including a fatal hit. The helper checks both current and recorded generations. Missing/expired history or a replaced body suppresses the historical effect; self-origin damage supplies no direction. This avoids inventing a bearing from later positions.

The same geometry places the hurt burst and spatial sound at the victim. The linked evidence records the fix for an earlier mapping that treated the damage origin as the victim's position. No gameplay, event, content or checkpoint schema changed. Direction nodes share the feedback ledger and scope cleanup, with a cap of 32 active indicators.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/wounds_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_WOUND_CAPTURE=/absolute/output/wound.png \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/wounds_run.sh

Evidence includes historical-position/generation tests, a live stationary-marker test and faulted three-peer revival. History is bounded to the existing proxy window; omitted feedback is counted. Browser visuals, hardware listening and wider failure cases remain part of full validation.

For wall effects, wall contacts retain explicit contact information from the simulation. Projectile disappearance alone cannot distinguish a wall hit from a body hit or timeout. Broader actor/menu behavior, other platforms, playtests and full comparison remain requirements.
